title: Food Labeling: How to Identify Conventional, Organic and GMO Produce
summary: Explains how produce PLU codes mark organic items and claims an 8 prefix marks genetically engineered produce.

assertions.quote: when you find the number nine in front of this four-digit code that means that the item is organically grown

verdicts.note: Under the IFPS convention, a 9 prefix on a four-digit PLU marks organic produce, though use is voluntary.

assertions.quote: if you happen to see the number eight in front of the four-digit number it means that the food is genetically engineered

verdicts.note: The 8 prefix was never adopted for GE produce, and IFPS has since dropped it and reassigns 8-series codes to new items.

assertions.quote: genetically engineered foods are not currently required to be labeled as such in the United States

verdicts.note: Since 2022 the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard has required disclosure of bioengineered foods, though with exemptions.

assertions.quote: certified organic products which cannot be genetically modified per regulations

verdicts.note: 7 CFR 205.105(e) says organic products must be made without excluded methods (the regulation's term for genetic engineering), the one exception being approved vaccines; 205.301(f)(1) applies the same rule to every ingredient labeled organic.
Quoting the National Organic Program: synthetic fertilizers, sewage sludge, irradiation and genetic engineering may not be used.
